events.title: France Abolishes Feudalism
events.description: In the early months of the French Revolution, the National Constituent Assembly voted to abolish feudalism in France. The decision dismantled the privileges of the nobility and clergy that had shaped rural life for centuries.
events.significance: It was a turning point of the Revolution. It replaced a system of inherited privilege with the principle of legal equality.

events.title: The Revenue Cutter Service Is Created
events.description: A newly passed tariff act created the Revenue Cutter Service. Its small fleet of armed vessels was meant to enforce customs laws and stop smuggling along the American coast.
events.significance: The service later grew into the United States Coast Guard, which still guards America's waters.

events.title: Anne Frank and Her Family Are Arrested
events.description: After an informant tipped off the authorities, the Gestapo raided the secret annex in Amsterdam. Eight people had been hiding there from the Nazis, including Anne Frank and her family.
events.significance: Anne's diary survived the war and became one of the most widely read personal accounts of the Holocaust.

events.title: Barack Obama Is Born
events.description: Barack Obama was born in Honolulu, Hawaii. He went on to become a community organizer, a law professor, a U.S. senator and, in 2008, president.
events.significance: He became the first African American elected President of the United States, a milestone in American history.

events.title: Missing Civil Rights Workers Found in Mississippi
events.description: The bodies of Michael Schwerner, Andrew Goodman and James Chaney were found in Mississippi. The three civil rights workers had disappeared on June 21 during the Freedom Summer voter registration campaign.
events.significance: Public outrage over the murders helped build support for the Civil Rights Act and the Voting Rights Act.
